programme.title: The Colours of China
programme.desc: Five colours are an integral part of contemporary China and the ancient philosophy of Wu Xing. Each episode takes us to regions where we meet our characters, learn how Wu Xing sits in their lives and explore the landscapes they live in.

programme.title: Facing Waves
programme.desc: Ken Whiting explores the remote and unforgiving coast of Lake Superior Provincial Park on a 5-day solo sea kayaking expedition - Part 1

programme.title: A Long Weekend in... With Rory O'Connell
programme.desc: Rory O’Connell’s brand new series combines travel and cookery with the popular chef enjoying the culture as well as the cuisine of eight European cities – Palma de Mallorca, Vienna, Lisbon, Madrid, Bath, Nantes, Copenhagen and Edinburgh. Rory visits a different city in each episode, and while the primary focus is on food, Rory is a knowledgeable guide to so much more, with art and design being particular interests of his. Food becomes much more interesting when seen in context – the culture it is part of the landscape it’s produced in, the history that has influenced it. At the end of each episode, Rory makes a delicious dish with the local produce which he sources on his travels.

programme.title: Epic Exploring
programme.desc: Urban explorer Cody Buffinton visits Morocco in search of an abandoned filmset in the Sahara Desert used for Game of Thrones.

programme.title: WaterVoyagers
programme.desc: Embark on a breathtaking voyage as WaterVoyagers makes its highly anticipated debut. This immersive travel series follows two American hosts, Tinabeth Pina and Frances Kuo, as they set sail on two Century Cruise ships along the legendary Yangtze River. From heart-racing adventures onshore to the lavish experiences aboard, WaterVoyagers offers a front-row seat to the ultimate travel escapade.

programme.title: Big Little Footprints
programme.desc: Sometimes exploring the road less traveled gives you the biggest adventure. In this episode, we escape the city buzz and opt for a quieter life on a Texas dude ranch. Taking time to appreciate the beauty in history, animals and quality time as a family.

programme.title: Going Beyond
programme.desc: Going Beyond is wanderlust-filled hitchhiker Mariia Khandus’s new travel project. She’s journeyed around the world. Everybody knows that Thailand, Vietnam, and Indonesia are great places to relax with wonderful beaches and delicious fruits! But what do you know about the local people? The expats? About the real lives of those living in these exotic countries? In our trip, we will discover it all, together! We visit the non-touristy places and show you the real Indochina! This is a set of stories of different people, through the prism of whom we show life in a country. It is a collection of diverse achievements, experiences and emotions. We are looking for the most interesting stories for you to keep expanding your own consciousness. Unbelievable panoramic views, interesting people, exciting stories and adventures – you’ll see all of this in our travel show, Going Beyond!

programme.title: The World Is Yours
programme.sub-title: The World Is Yours - Marrakech, Philadelphia, Barbados & Martinique
programme.desc: We will go to the bustling city of Marrakech, where we will explore the citadel and the exciting market of La Medina, before moving out of the city towards the Ksar of Ait Ben Haddou, the wonderful Atlas mountains, the dunes of Merzouga and there we'll try the Couscous a rich dish of Moroccan food. Then we will go to Philadelphia, in the USA, where we will tour Independence Hall, the impressive City Hall building and a creepy historic prison. And before we go to our next destination, we will have an aperitif, the delicious hoagies sandwiches, also known as submarine sandwich. Our last destination of the day will be the Caribbean islands of Barbados, where we will make a catamaran cruise, visit the capital Bridgetown and finally move to Martinique, home to some incredible beaches and French cultural influences.

programme.desc: Cycling through some of Ireland’s most stunning scenery, chef Neven Maguire explores established Greenways such as The Great Western Greenway in Mayo, The Limerick, Waterford and Royal Canal Greenways; and he follows the routes of future Greenways planned for South Kerry and Connemara in Co. Galway. Along the way Neven meets some of Ireland’s most talented food producers and chefs in a variety of interesting locations. Ireland’s Greenways follow the routes of abandoned railway lines and canals which have been revitalised as cycling and walking tracks, passing through dramatic mountainous landscapes, lakeshores and seascapes. On his travels Neven also meets local historians who tell him all about these 19th century feats of engineering which had a transformative impact on the whole country. Many of the original aqueducts, viaducts and tunnels form part of the Greenways today and feature in the series.
